findings.title: The "Caching" tests were deleted instead of updated.
findings.body: This hunk deletes the whole `describe("Caching")` block, which covered `getAuthorizationConditions` and `getFilterConditions`. Those tests still apply after the change: the service still caches results in `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`. Only their expected values needed to become `Prisma.sql` values. Now nothing catches a broken cache, such as a `null` filter result being rebuilt on every call or the auth query running on every call. The request only asked to move the expectations to the new format. Fix: put both tests back and change their expectations to `Prisma.sql`, as the other tests now do.

findings.title: The new public options type no longer catches a team scope without `teamId` at compile time.
findings.body: The constructor now takes `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, which allows `scope: "team"` with no `teamId` and accepts any mix of fields. The old type was the discriminated union inferred from zod. With the new type, a caller that leaves out `teamId` compiles cleanly. At runtime zod validation then fails, so `options` becomes null and every query silently returns no rows (`1=0`). Fix: keep `InsightsBookingServiceOptions` as the constructor's parameter type.

held.title: Removing the public `findMany` method can break existing callers.
held.body: `findMany(findManyArgs)` is removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns raw SQL. The old method merged the caller's `where` with the auth and filter conditions. Any existing caller, such as an insights tRPC router, will now fail to compile or hit an undefined method at runtime. Moving such a caller to raw SQL also means it must apply the authorization condition itself. I could not see the call sites from here. Fix: check every `findMany` call site and update it in this PR, or keep a wrapper until they are migrated.
